mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financial conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such Fed rate spikes, or the S&P 500 shows no mean reversion to the pre-rate hike trend.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% over the prior month coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as stronger wage growth boosts consumer confidence and investment.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) over the 60-day window following such pay growth acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% in two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals weakening manufacturing demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% in two consecutive months prior to prediction
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during such double-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 216 for three consecutive months indicates a disinflationary environment that supports a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: No significant positive return (p > 0.05) in the 20-day window following such CPI behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 6% for two consecutive months, it coincides with a positive S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates continued economic expansion.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during such UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both Home Sales (HOUST) and Retail Sales (not available in catalog—skip) is replaced by a rise in RSAFS (retail sales proxy) above 400,000 and HOUST above 700, that triggers a positive S&P 20-day return via dual demand channels.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return (p > 0.05) when both proxies exceed thresholds simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining labor participation (PAYEMS falling for four consecutive months) predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return as it reflects weak labor market expansion and reduced consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreasing for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such participation declines.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1% for three consecutive months), the S&P 20-day forward return tends to be positive as markets anticipate continued easing and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the three-month easing streak.
